prompt:
TESSERA STYLE SHEET
1. Modern editorial paper collage: bold magazine composition, refined 2D motion design, photographed flat under soft room light.
2. One flat block-colour paper ground fills the frame: deep magenta. The ground is a single unbroken colour.
3. Subjects are black-and-white halftone photographic cutouts with rough white torn-paper edges: objects, machines, buildings, maps, coins, screens, vehicles, anonymous paper hands. Every cutout is a plain, unmarked object: calendar pages, documents, coins, screens and vehicles are blank and unprinted, with no lettering, numerals, symbols, liveries or marks on them. Every cutout is matte paper reflecting only the room light, with a plain blank face: coin rims, document faces, screens and vehicle sides carry no lettering, numerals or marks.
4. Diagram elements are flat matte paper shapes and ribbons, tape, rubber stamps, string and pins, stencilled arrows, paper bar charts, stacked sheets, grid paper, torn strips, hole-punched tags, paper clips, in cream, black, pale yellow or the ground's contrasting colour, with real paper texture and print dots.
5. One consistent light from the upper left; each paper layer casts a small soft shadow.
6. Layout: the headline chip owns the upper third of the frame and stays uncovered; subjects and diagrams occupy the lower two-thirds. When the frame opens on a previous composition, its elements slide off or are covered in the first second and the new headline lands on clear ground.
7. Headline typography: one extra-bold sans-serif in black or cream, printed on a cream or black paper chip: one line, no wider than a third of the frame width, with safe margins, the chip sitting clear of the subjects. Letterforms are accurate, complete and stable from the frame they appear in; the chip is printed once and does not redraw. When the beat marks a hero number, that number alone may be printed larger, up to half the frame width.
8. Compositions vary in scale from beat to beat: some show one oversized subject filling the frame, some a small subject alone on open ground, some several elements arranged as a diagram.
9. Motion: elements enter fast with slight overshoot and a stable landing, then hold a clear reading window; one strongest focus at a time; the camera is locked; movement starts on the first frame and a small loop continues at the end; no empty frames.
10. 16:9, exactly 5 seconds, one composition, at most one crisp cut.
11. Identity anchor: rough white torn edges on every cutout; small paper shadow from the upper-left light.

BEAT
Ground: deep magenta.
Subjects: a paper calendar strip; paper coins.
Opens on the arrow, carried over from the previous shot, which transforms as the action begins.
Action: The previous chip flips away as the arrow unrolls into a paper calendar strip; coins slide off it month by month.
Ends holding on the strip.
This composition is a diagram: several elements are arranged together.
Headline printed on a paper chip: "$1.3M / MONTH".

ON-SCREEN TEXT: "$1.3M / MONTH". This string is printed complete and correct from its first visible frame and never changes. It is the only lettering in the frame.

AUDIO: One English narrator, warm, clear, natural, brisk but unhurried, never an advertising shout. Speak the following line exactly once, word for word, beginning on the first frame: "Operating burn ran about one point three million a month.". No other dialogue. Light paper-slap and tape sound effects beneath the voice; no music.

integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] This is a modern editorial paper collage style, photographed flat under soft room light. The scene opens on <Picture 1>, where a deep magenta paper ground fills the frame. An existing cream paper chip with black text and a black-and-white halftone arrow are visible. A consistent light source from the upper left casts small, soft shadows beneath every layer. Immediately, a male narrator (S1), with a warm, clear, and natural mid-range timbre and a brisk but unhurried speaking rate, says: <d>[English] Operating burn ran about one point three million a month.</d> Simultaneously, the existing headline chip from the first frame flips away quickly with a slight overshoot, and the halftone arrow unrolls with a snappy, 2D motion design into a long, vertical paper calendar strip. This strip is a black-and-white halftone cutout with rough white torn-paper edges; the calendar faces are entirely blank, with no printed numbers or dates. As the strip settles, several circular paper coin cutouts, also in black-and-white halftone with rough white torn edges and blank faces, slide off the strip one by one in a rhythmic sequence, moving downward across the magenta ground. In the upper third of the frame, a new cream paper chip lands firmly on the clear ground, featuring the extra-bold black sans-serif text "$1.3M / MONTH". The text is clean, legible, and stable. The camera remains in a Static Shot throughout the 5 seconds. The action concludes with the composition holding steadily on the calendar strip, the scattered coins, and the headline chip.

overall_soundscape: The audio is dominated by a clean vocal recording. Beneath the voice, there are rhythmic, tactile foley sounds: a crisp paper-slap as the chip flips, a textured sliding sound as the calendar unrolls, and several light, percussive "taps" of paper hitting paper as the coins slide off.
